Google has introduced the new online payment wallets named Tez. Tez, which means fast, is launched for the Indian smartphone users market. Google unveils Tez to tap into one of the world’s fastest-growing smartphone market. The new my wallet app will help the users connect their phones with their bank accounts. The smartphone users can use the online payment wallets for making online purchases and in physical stores. Furthermore, the users can also use the online payment wallets to transfer money to other users.

Google on the Tez Online Payment Wallets

In a statement, Google has revealed how the users can take benefit of this new application. In a statement, the search engine giant stated that friends could use this app to split dinner bill. Similarly, the users can make simpler payments like paying the chaiwallah. Google wants Indians to replace cash by using its mobile application. The users will be able to make big and small payments by using Tez. The using of Audio QR will let the uses have their phones talk to each other. The idea is to make the process convenient and easy to follow.

Linking to the Application with UPI

The new Tez application is launched for the iOS and Android mobile operating systems. The application will rely on the Unified Payments Interface. Many banks in India offer support for the UPI. However, a lot of them are still making efforts to provide support for this payment interface. The application will come pre-installed on Android phones made by Panasonic, Micromax, Nokia, and Lava.

Tez App is Free for Now

For now, Google will not charge any money for the payment transfers. The small merchants and consumers do not need to make any payments. However, experts believe that once the application becomes widely available to users, the company will start charging a nominal fee. Tez is different from PayTM that already has over 200 million registered users in India. The PayTM is a mobile wallet where the app users need to save money. However, in case of Tez, the users do not need to save any money in the wallet. The direct linking of the bank account with the wallet eliminates one additional step of saving money into the wallet. Thus, Google’s Tez mobile app for India is more efficient than PayTM. The banks currently supporting UPI include HDFC Bank, Axis, and State Bank of India.
